"""Assembly of the full appctl command tree."""

from ..registry import CommandRegistry
from . import cache, cli, config, db, help, option, plugin, post, site, theme, user

COMMAND_MODULES = (cache, cli, config, db, help, option, plugin, post, site, theme, user)


def build_command_tree():
    registry = CommandRegistry(description="Manage applications from the command line.")
    for module in COMMAND_MODULES:
        module.register(registry)
    return registry.root
"""``appctl cli``: information about appctl itself."""

import os
import platform

from .. import PROGRAM_NAME, __version__, upgrade
from ..arguments import is_assoc_token, parse_assoc_token
from ..formatter import format_value
from ..errors import AppctlError
from ..extract import extract_archive, validate_archive
from ..resolver import try_resolve
from ..runtime_config import GLOBAL_PARAMETERS, visible_parameters
from ..synopsis import ASSOC, FLAG


def version(ctx, args, assoc):
    ctx.output.line(f"{PROGRAM_NAME} {__version__}")


def info(ctx, args, assoc):
    data = {
        "appctl_version": __version__,
        "python_version": platform.python_version(),
        "os": platform.system(),
        "strict_args_mode": ctx.strict,
        "global_config_path": ctx.config.global_path if ctx.config else None,
        "project_config_path": ctx.config.project_path if ctx.config else None,
        "packages_dir": ctx.config.packages_dir if ctx.config else None,
        "runtime_config": {k: v for k, v in ctx.runtime.items()
                           if v != GLOBAL_PARAMETERS[k].default},
    }
    if assoc["format"] == "json":
        ctx.output.line(format_value(data, "json"))
        return
    if assoc["format"] != "list":
        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid format: {assoc['format']}. Supported formats: list, json.")
    ctx.output.line(f"appctl version:\t{data['appctl_version']}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Python version:\t{data['python_version']}")
    ctx.output.line(f"OS:\t{data['os']}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Strict args mode:\t{'enabled' if ctx.strict else 'disabled'}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Global config:\t{data['global_config_path'] or ''}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Project config:\t{data['project_config_path'] or ''}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Packages dir:\t{data['packages_dir'] or ''}")
    for key, value in data["runtime_config"].items():
        ctx.output.line(f"--{key}:\t{format_value(value)}")


def update(ctx, args, assoc):
    archive = assoc.get("archive")
    validate_archive(archive)
    dest = assoc.get("path") or ctx.runtime.get("path") or os.getcwd()
    if dest is True:
        raise AppctlError("--path parameter needs a value.")
    dest = extract_archive(archive, str(dest), ctx.output)
    ctx.output.success(f"Extracted '{archive}' to '{dest}'.")


def migrate(ctx, args, assoc):
    upgrade.run_upgrade(ctx.environ, ctx.output)
    ctx.output.success(f"Upgraded to {PROGRAM_NAME} {__version__}.")


def param_dump(ctx, args, assoc):
    dump = {}
    for name, param in visible_parameters().items():
        entry = {"synopsis": param.synopsis, "description": param.description,
                 "default": param.default}
        if assoc.get("with-values"):
            entry["current"] = ctx.runtime.get(name)
        dump[name] = entry
    ctx.output.line(format_value(dump, "json"))


def has_command(ctx, args, assoc):
    tokens = " ".join(args).split()
    resolved = try_resolve(ctx.root, tokens)
    found = resolved is not None and not resolved[1]
    return 0 if found else 1


def _completion_words(line):
    """Split the line into completed words and the word being typed."""
    words = line.split()
    current = words.pop() if words and not line[-1].isspace() else ""
    if words and os.path.basename(words[0]) in (PROGRAM_NAME, f"{PROGRAM_NAME}.py"):
        words = words[1:]
    elif not words and os.path.basename(current) in (PROGRAM_NAME, f"{PROGRAM_NAME}.py"):
        current = ""
    return words, current


def completion_candidates(root, line):
    words, current = _completion_words(line)
    used = {parse_assoc_token(w)[0] for w in words if is_assoc_token(w)}
    command = root
    consumed = True
    for word in (w for w in words if not is_assoc_token(w)):
        child = command.find_subcommand(word) if consumed else None
        if child is None:
            if not command.is_runnable or command.is_root:
                return []
            consumed = False
            continue
        command = child
    candidates = []
    if consumed:
        candidates += [f"{sub.name} " for sub in command.sorted_subcommands()]
    if command.is_runnable and not command.is_root:
        for token in command.tokens_of_type(ASSOC, FLAG):
            if token.name not in used:
                candidates.append(f"--{token.name}=" if token.type == ASSOC else f"--{token.name} ")
        for name, param in visible_parameters().items():
            if param.runtime and name not in used:
                candidates.append(f"--{name}=" if "=" in param.synopsis else f"--{name} ")
    return [c for c in candidates if c.startswith(current)]


def completions(ctx, args, assoc):
    line = str(assoc["line"])
    point = assoc.get("point")
    if point is not None and point is not True:
        try:
            line = line[:int(point)]
        except ValueError:
            pass
    for candidate in completion_candidates(ctx.root, line):
        ctx.output.line(candidate)


def register(registry):
    registry.add("cli", description="Reviews current appctl info.")
    registry.add("cli version", version, description="Prints the appctl version.")
    registry.add(
        "cli info", info,
        synopsis="[--format=<format>]",
        description="Prints various details about the appctl environment.",
        defaults={"format": "list"},
        options={"format": "Render output in a particular format (list, json)."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli update", update,
        synopsis="--archive=<archive-path> [--path=<destination>]",
        description="Extracts a .zip or .tar.gz archive into a directory.",
        options={"archive": "Path to the archive to extract.",
                 "path": "Directory to extract into. Defaults to the current directory."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli migrate", migrate,
        description="Runs pending migrations and upgrades containers to the current version.",
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli param-dump", param_dump,
        synopsis="[--with-values] [--format=<format>]",
        description="Dumps the list of global parameters, as JSON.",
        defaults={"format": "json"},
        options={"with-values": "Display current values also."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli completions", completions,
        synopsis="--line=<line> [--point=<point>]",
        description="Generates tab completion strings.",
        options={"line": "The current command line to be executed.",
                 "point": "The index to the current cursor position relative to the beginning "
                          "of the command."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli has-command", has_command,
        synopsis="<command-name>...",
        description="Detects if a command exists.",
        options={"command-name": "The command to check."},
    )
"""``appctl help``: show help for any command."""

from ..help import render_command_help, render_root_help
from ..resolver import resolve


def help_command(ctx, args, assoc):
    if not args:
        ctx.output.line(render_root_help(ctx.root))
        return
    command, _ = resolve(ctx.root, args)
    ctx.output.line(render_command_help(command))


def register(registry):
    registry.add(
        "help", help_command,
        synopsis="[<command>...]",

"""``appctl cli``: information about appctl itself."""

import os
import platform

from .. import PROGRAM_NAME, __version__, upgrade
from ..arguments import is_assoc_token, parse_assoc_token
from ..formatter import format_value
from ..errors import AppctlError
from ..extract import extract_archive, validate_archive
from ..resolver import try_resolve
from ..runtime_config import GLOBAL_PARAMETERS, visible_parameters
from ..synopsis import ASSOC, FLAG


def version(ctx, args, assoc):
    ctx.output.line(f"{PROGRAM_NAME} {__version__}")


def info(ctx, args, assoc):
    data = {
        "appctl_version": __version__,
        "python_version": platform.python_version(),
        "os": platform.system(),
        "strict_args_mode": ctx.strict,
        "global_config_path": ctx.config.global_path if ctx.config else None,
        "project_config_path": ctx.config.project_path if ctx.config else None,
        "packages_dir": ctx.config.packages_dir if ctx.config else None,
        "runtime_config": {k: v for k, v in ctx.runtime.items()
                           if v != GLOBAL_PARAMETERS[k].default},
    }
    if assoc["format"] == "json":
        ctx.output.line(format_value(data, "json"))
        return
    if assoc["format"] != "list":
        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid format: {assoc['format']}. Supported formats: list, json.")
    ctx.output.line(f"appctl version:\t{data['appctl_version']}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Python version:\t{data['python_version']}")
    ctx.output.line(f"OS:\t{data['os']}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Strict args mode:\t{'enabled' if ctx.strict else 'disabled'}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Global config:\t{data['global_config_path'] or ''}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Project config:\t{data['project_config_path'] or ''}")
    ctx.output.line(f"Packages dir:\t{data['packages_dir'] or ''}")
    for key, value in data["runtime_config"].items():
        ctx.output.line(f"--{key}:\t{format_value(value)}")


def update(ctx, args, assoc):
    archive = assoc.get("archive")
    validate_archive(archive)
    dest = assoc.get("path") or ctx.runtime.get("path") or os.getcwd()
    if dest is True:
        raise AppctlError("--path parameter needs a value.")
    dest = extract_archive(archive, str(dest), ctx.output)
    ctx.output.success(f"Extracted '{archive}' to '{dest}'.")


def migrate(ctx, args, assoc):
    upgrade.run_upgrade(ctx.environ, ctx.output)
    ctx.output.success(f"Upgraded to {PROGRAM_NAME} {__version__}.")


def param_dump(ctx, args, assoc):
    dump = {}
    for name, param in visible_parameters().items():
        entry = {"synopsis": param.synopsis, "description": param.description,
                 "default": param.default}
        if assoc.get("with-values"):
            entry["current"] = ctx.runtime.get(name)
        dump[name] = entry
    ctx.output.line(format_value(dump, "json"))


def has_command(ctx, args, assoc):
    tokens = " ".join(args).split()
    resolved = try_resolve(ctx.root, tokens)
    found = resolved is not None and not resolved[1]
    return 0 if found else 1


def _completion_words(line):
    """Split the line into completed words and the word being typed."""
    words = line.split()
    current = words.pop() if words and not line[-1].isspace() else ""
    if words and os.path.basename(words[0]) in (PROGRAM_NAME, f"{PROGRAM_NAME}.py"):
        words = words[1:]
    elif not words and os.path.basename(current) in (PROGRAM_NAME, f"{PROGRAM_NAME}.py"):
        current = ""
    return words, current


def completion_candidates(root, line):
    words, current = _completion_words(line)
    used = {parse_assoc_token(w)[0] for w in words if is_assoc_token(w)}
    command = root
    consumed = True
    for word in (w for w in words if not is_assoc_token(w)):
        child = command.find_subcommand(word) if consumed else None
        if child is None:
            if not command.is_runnable or command.is_root:
                return []
            consumed = False
            continue
        command = child
    candidates = []
    if consumed:
        candidates += [f"{sub.name} " for sub in command.sorted_subcommands()]
    if command.is_runnable and not command.is_root:
        for token in command.tokens_of_type(ASSOC, FLAG):
            if token.name not in used:
                candidates.append(f"--{token.name}=" if token.type == ASSOC else f"--{token.name} ")
        for name, param in visible_parameters().items():
            if param.runtime and name not in used:
                candidates.append(f"--{name}=" if "=" in param.synopsis else f"--{name} ")
    return [c for c in candidates if c.startswith(current)]


def completions(ctx, args, assoc):
    line = str(assoc["line"])
    point = assoc.get("point")
    if point is not None and point is not True:
        try:
            line = line[:int(point)]
        except ValueError:
            pass
    for candidate in completion_candidates(ctx.root, line):
        ctx.output.line(candidate)


def register(registry):
    registry.add("cli", description="Reviews current appctl info.")
    registry.add("cli version", version, description="Prints the appctl version.")
    registry.add(
        "cli info", info,
        synopsis="[--format=<format>]",
        description="Prints various details about the appctl environment.",
        defaults={"format": "list"},
        options={"format": "Render output in a particular format (list, json)."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli update", update,
        synopsis="--archive=<archive-path> [--path=<destination>]",
        description="Extracts a .zip or .tar.gz archive into a directory.",
        options={"archive": "Path to the archive to extract.",
                 "path": "Directory to extract into. Defaults to the current directory."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli migrate", migrate,
        description="Runs pending migrations and upgrades containers to the current version.",
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli param-dump", param_dump,
        synopsis="[--with-values] [--format=<format>]",
        description="Dumps the list of global parameters, as JSON.",
        defaults={"format": "json"},
        options={"with-values": "Display current values also."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli completions", completions,
        synopsis="--line=<line> [--point=<point>]",
        description="Generates tab completion strings.",
        options={"line": "The current command line to be executed.",
                 "point": "The index to the current cursor position relative to the beginning "
                          "of the command."},
    )
    registry.add(
        "cli has-command", has_command,
        synopsis="<command-name>...",
        description="Detects if a command exists.",
        options={"command-name": "The command to check."},
    )
"""``appctl help``: show help for any command."""

from ..help import render_command_help, render_root_help
from ..resolver import resolve


def help_command(ctx, args, assoc):
    if not args:
        ctx.output.line(render_root_help(ctx.root))
        return
    command, _ = resolve(ctx.root, args)
    ctx.output.line(render_command_help(command))


def register(registry):
    registry.add(
        "help", help_command,
        synopsis="[<command>...]",
        description="Gets help for appctl commands.",
        options={"command": "Get help on a specific command."},
    )

"""End-to-end tests running appctl.py as a subprocess."""

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))
SCRIPT = os.path.join(ROOT, "appctl.py")


def run(*args, strict=False):
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"}
    if strict:
        env["APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"] = "1"
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, SCRIPT, *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                          env=env, cwd=ROOT)


class CliTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_no_arguments_lists_commands_sorted_and_aligned(self):
        result = run()
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        rows = [m for m in re.finditer(r"^  (\S+)( +)(\S.*)$", result.stdout, re.M)]
        names = [m.group(1) for m in rows]
        self.assertIn("site", names)
        self.assertEqual(names, sorted(names, key=str.lower))
        columns = {len(m.group(1)) + len(m.group(2)) for m in rows}
        self.assertEqual(len(columns), 1)

    def test_unknown_command(self):
        result = run("sitee")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, (
            "Error: 'sitee' is not a registered appctl command. "
            "See 'appctl help' for available commands.\nDid you mean 'site'?\n"))
        self.assertEqual(result.stdout, "")

    def test_unknown_command_without_suggestion(self):
        result = run("qqqqqq")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertNotIn("Did you mean", result.stderr)

    def test_unknown_subcommand(self):
        result = run("site", "craete")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, (
            "Error: 'craete' is not a registered subcommand of 'site'. "
            "See 'appctl help site' for available subcommands.\nDid you mean 'create'?\n"))

    def test_synonym_suggestion(self):
        self.assertIn("Did you mean 'create'?", run("site", "new").stderr)

    def test_alias_wins_over_synonym(self):
        result = run("user", "remove", "2")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertNotIn("Did you mean", result.stderr)
        self.assertIn("Removed user 2", result.stdout)

    def test_parent_without_handler_prints_usage(self):
        result = run("site")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("usage: appctl site activate", result.stdout)
        self.assertIn("   or: appctl site create", result.stdout)

    def test_missing_positional_prints_usage(self):
        result = run("site", "create")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertTrue(result.stdout.startswith("usage: appctl site create <site-name>"))

    def test_too_many_positionals(self):
        result = run("site", "create", "a", "b")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, "Error: Too many positional arguments: b\n")

    def test_missing_required_assoc(self):
        result = run("config", "create", "--dbname=x", "--dbuser=")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, "Error: Parameter errors:\n missing --dbuser parameter\n")

    def test_unknown_assoc_with_suggestion(self):
        result = run("site", "create", "x", "--typ=a", "--bogus")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, (
            "Error: Parameter errors:\n unknown --typ parameter\nDid you mean '--type'?\n"
            " unknown --bogus parameter\n"))

    def test_defaults_applied(self):
        result = run("site", "create", "x")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        self.assertIn("type: standard", result.stdout)

    def test_no_prefix_sets_false(self):
        self.assertIn("visibility: public", run("site", "create", "x", "--no-private").stdout)
        self.assertIn("visibility: private", run("site", "create", "x", "--private").stdout)

    def test_help_rewrite(self):
        self.assertEqual(run("site", "create", "--help").stdout, run("help", "site", "create").stdout)
        self.assertIn("SYNOPSIS", run("site", "create", "--help").stdout)

    def test_version_rewrite(self):
        result = run("--version")
        self.assertEqual((result.returncode, result.stdout), (0, run("cli", "version").stdout))

    def test_strict_mode(self):
        self.assertEqual(run("site", "create", "x", "--url=a").returncode, 0)
        strict = run("site", "create", "x", "--url=a", strict=True)
        self.assertEqual(strict.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn("unknown --url parameter", strict.stderr)
        self.assertEqual(run("--url=a", "site", "create", "x", strict=True).returncode, 0)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
import unittest

from appctl_cli.arguments import parse_argv
from appctl_cli.errors import AppctlError, CommandNotFoundError, UsageError
from appctl_cli.registry import CommandRegistry
from appctl_cli.resolver import resolve
from appctl_cli.rewrites import apply_rewrites
from appctl_cli.validator import ArgumentValidator


def handler(ctx, args, assoc):
    return 0


class ArgumentParsingTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_split(self):
        parsed = parse_argv(["site", "create", "x", "--type=a", "--force", "--no-color", "--url=u"])
        self.assertEqual(parsed.positional, ["site", "create", "x"])
        self.assertEqual(parsed.assoc, {"type": "a", "force": True})
        self.assertEqual(parsed.runtime, {"color": False, "url": "u"})

    def test_strict_mode(self):
        parsed = parse_argv(["--url=a", "site", "--url=b"], strict=True)
        self.assertEqual(parsed.runtime, {"url": "a"})
        self.assertEqual(parsed.assoc, {"url": "b"})

    def test_end_of_options(self):
        parsed = parse_argv(["db", "query", "--", "--weird"])
        self.assertEqual(parsed.positional, ["db", "query", "--weird"])


class RewriteTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_help(self):
        self.assertEqual(apply_rewrites(["site", "create", "--help"]), ["help", "site", "create"])
        self.assertEqual(apply_rewrites(["--help"]), ["help"])

    def test_version(self):
        self.assertEqual(apply_rewrites(["--version"]), ["cli", "version"])
        self.assertEqual(apply_rewrites(["plugin", "install", "x", "--version=1"]),
                         ["plugin", "install", "x", "--version=1"])


class ResolverTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        registry = CommandRegistry()
        registry.add("site", description="Sites")
        registry.add("site create", handler, synopsis="<name>", alias="make")
        registry.add("tool", handler, synopsis="[<arg>]")
        registry.add("tool sub", handler)
        self.root = registry.root

    def test_deepest_match(self):
        command, rest = resolve(self.root, ["site", "create", "x"])
        self.assertEqual((command.full_name, rest), ("site create", ["x"]))

    def test_alias(self):
        command, _ = resolve(self.root, ["site", "make", "x"])
        self.assertEqual(command.full_name, "site create")

    def test_runnable_parent_keeps_unmatched_tokens(self):
        command, rest = resolve(self.root, ["tool", "value"])
        self.assertEqual((command.full_name, rest), ("tool", ["value"]))

    def test_unknown(self):
        with self.assertRaises(CommandNotFoundError) as ctx:

import os
import re
import subprocess
import sys
import unittest

ROOT = os.path.dirname(os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__)))

def run(*args, strict=False):
    env = {k: v for k, v in os.environ.items() if k != "APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"}
    if strict:
        env["APPCTL_STRICT_ARGS_MODE"] = "1"
    return subprocess.run([sys.executable, SCRIPT, *args], capture_output=True, text=True,
                          env=env, cwd=ROOT)


class CliTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_no_arguments_lists_commands_sorted_and_aligned(self):
        result = run()
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 0)
        rows = [m for m in re.finditer(r"^  (\S+)( +)(\S.*)$", result.stdout, re.M)]
        names = [m.group(1) for m in rows]
        self.assertIn("site", names)
        self.assertEqual(names, sorted(names, key=str.lower))
        columns = {len(m.group(1)) + len(m.group(2)) for m in rows}
        self.assertEqual(len(columns), 1)

    def test_unknown_command(self):
        result = run("sitee")
        self.assertEqual(result.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(result.stderr, (

            "See 'appctl help' for available commands.\nDid you mean 'site'?\n"))

267	    accepts = any(p.kind in (p.POSITIONAL_ONLY, p.POSITIONAL_OR_KEYWORD, p.VAR_POSITIONAL)
268	                  for p in parameters)
269	    return function(context) if accepts else function()
270	
271	
272	class MigrationBatch:
273	    """Runs pending migrations of one type; a failure rolls back the batch."""
274	
275	    def __init__(self, type, db, output=None, environ=None):
276	        self.type = type
277	        self.db = db
278	        self.output = _output(output)
279	        self.environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
280	        self.processor = RevertableStepProcessor(self.output, f"{type} migrations")
281	        self.applied = []
282	
283	    def run(self):
284	        """Apply every pending migration; return the identities that ran."""
285	        pending = pending_migrations(self.db, self.type, self.environ)
286	        for artifact in pending:
287	            state = {}
288	            self.processor.add_step(artifact.identity, self._up, self._down,
289	                                    (artifact, state), (artifact, state))
290	        if self.processor.execute():
291	            return list(self.applied)
292	        error = self.processor.error
293	        if isinstance(error, MigrationFileNotFound):
294	            self.output.error(error.message)
295	        else:
296	            step = self.processor.failed_step
297	            reason = error.message if isinstance(error, AppctlError) else str(error) or repr(error)
298	            self.output.error(f"Migration '{step.id}' failed: {reason}")
299	        raise ReportedError(MIGRATION_ERROR)
300	
301	    def rollback(self):
302	        self.processor.rollback()
303	
304	    def _context(self, artifact):
305	        return MigrationContext(self.db, self.output, self.environ, artifact)
306	
307	    def _up(self, artifact, state):
308	        self.output.debug(f"Running {self.type} migration: {artifact.identity}", group="upgrade")
309	        up, state["down"] = load_migration(artifact)
310	        _call(up, self._context(artifact))
311	        state["done"] = True
312	        self.db.record_migration(artifact.identity, self.type)
313	        self.applied.append(artifact.identity)
314	
315	    def _down(self, artifact, state):
316	        if not state.pop("done", False):
317	            return
318	        self.output.debug(f"Reverting {self.type} migration: {artifact.identity}", group="upgrade")
319	        try:
320	            if state.get("down") is not None:
321	                _call(state["down"], self._context(artifact))
322	        finally:
323	            self.db.remove_migration(artifact.identity, self.type)
324	            if artifact.identity in self.applied:
325	                self.applied.remove(artifact.identity)
326

328	# -- image versions ----------------------------------------------------------------------
329	
330	
331	def split_image(reference):
332	    """``(repository, tag)`` of an image reference; the tag may be ``None``."""
333	    reference = str(reference).split("@", 1)[0]
334	    slash, colon = reference.rfind("/"), reference.rfind(":")
335	    if colon > slash:
336	        return reference[:colon], reference[colon + 1:]
337	    return reference, None
338	
339	
340	def target_image_versions(path=None):
341	    """``{image: tag}`` of the images managed by this appctl version."""
342	    with open(path or IMAGE_VERSIONS_FILE, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
343	        data = json.load(handle)
344	    return {str(image): str(tag) for image, tag in sorted(data.items())}
345	
346	
347	def local_image_tags(output=None):
348	    """``{repository: {tags}}`` of the images present in the container runtime."""
349	    result = run_command([container.RUNTIME_BINARY, "images", "--format",
350	                          "{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}}"], output)
351	    tags = {}
352	    if result.succeeded:
353	        for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
354	            repository, tag = split_image(line.strip())
355	            if repository and tag and tag != "<none>":
356	                tags.setdefault(repository, set()).add(tag)
357	    return tags
358	
359	
360	def current_image_versions(db, targets, output=None):
361	    """Version in use per image: the recorded one, else the one observed locally."""
362	    current = {}
363	    observed = None
364	    for image, target in targets.items():
365	        stored = db.get_option(image)
366	        if stored is not False:
367	            current[image] = stored
368	            continue
369	        if observed is None:
370	            observed = local_image_tags(output) if shutil.which(container.RUNTIME_BINARY) else {}
371	        tags = observed.get(image, set())
372	        current[image] = target if target in tags else (sorted(tags)[-1] if tags else None)
373	    return current
374	
375	
376	def changed_images(current, targets):
377	    """Images whose version differs (exact tag comparison), with their new tag, by name."""
378	    return {image: tag for image, tag in sorted(targets.items()) if current.get(image) != tag}
379	
380	
381	def pull_images(changed, output=None):
382	    """Pull the new images one after the other; stop at the first failure."""
383	    output = _output(output)
384	    for image, tag in changed.items():
385	        reference = f"{image}:{tag}"
386	        output.debug(f"Pulling image {reference}", group="upgrade")
387	        if not exec_command([container.RUNTIME_BINARY, "pull", reference], output):
388	            output.error(f"Unable to pull {reference}. Please check logs for more details.")
389	            raise ReportedError(MIGRATION_ERROR)
390	
391	
392	# -- compose projects ------------------------------------------------------------------------
393	
394	_IMAGE_RE = re.compile(
395	    r"(?P<pre>\bimage\s*:\s*(?P<q>[\"']?))(?P<ref>[^\s\"'#,{}\[\]]+?)(?P=q)"
396	    r"(?=\s|,|\}|#|$)", re.MULTILINE)
397	
398	
399	def affected_services(config, changed):
400	    """``{service: image repository}`` of the services using a changed image."""
401	    affected = {}
402	    for name, service in ((config or {}).get("services") or {}).items():
403	        image = service.get("image") if isinstance(service, dict) else None
404	        if image:
405	            repository, _ = split_image(image)
406	            if repository in changed:
407	                affected[str(name)] = repository
408	    return affected
409	
410	
411	def rewrite_images(text, changed):
412	    """Compose file text with every changed image set to its new tag."""
413	    def replace(match):
414	        repository, _ = split_image(match.group("ref"))
415	        if repository not in changed:
416	            return match.group(0)
417	        return f"{match.group('pre')}{repository}:{changed[repository]}{match.group('q')}"
418	    return _IMAGE_RE.sub(replace, text)
419	
420	
421	class ComposeUpgrade:
422	    """Revertable replacement of the services of one compose project using changed images."""
423	
424	    def __init__(self, label, project_dir, project, changed, output=None):
425	        self.label = label
426	        self.project_dir = project_dir
427	        self.project = project
428	        self.changed = changed
429	        self.output = _output(output)
430	        self.files = container.compose_files(project_dir, output=self.output)
431	        self.services = affected_services(container.load_compose_config(self.files), changed)
432	        self.originals = {}
433	        self.processor = RevertableStepProcessor(self.output, label)
434	
435	    @property
436	    def needed(self):
437	        return bool(self.services)
438	
439	    def run(self):
440	        self.processor.add_step(f"{self.label}: update compose files", self._rewrite,
441	                                self._restore_files)
442	        self.processor.add_step(f"{self.label}: replace containers", self._up,
443	                                self._restore_containers)
444	        if not self.processor.execute():
445	            error = self.processor.error
446	            reason = error.message if isinstance(error, AppctlError) else str(error)
447	            self.output.error(f"Unable to upgrade the containers of {self.label}: {reason}")
448	            raise ReportedError(MIGRATION_ERROR)
449	
450	    def rollback(self):
451	        self.processor.rollback()
452	
453	    def _rewrite(self):
454	        for path in self.files:
455	            with open(path, encoding="utf-8") as handle:
456	                text = handle.read()
457	            updated = rewrite_images(text, self.changed)
458	            if updated != text:
459	                self.originals[path] = text
460	                with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
461	                    handle.write(updated)
462	        config = container.load_compose_config(self.files)
463	        for service in self.services:
464	            image = config["services"][service].get("image")
465	            repository, tag = split_image(image)
466	            if tag != self.changed[repository]:
467	                raise AppctlError(f"Unable to update the image of the '{service}' service.")
468	
469	    def _restore_files(self):
470	        for path, text in self.originals.items():
471	            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
472	                handle.write(text)
473	
474	    def _up(self):
475	        argv = container.compose_command(self.project_dir, output=self.output,
476	                                         project=self.project)
477	        argv += ["up", "-d", "--no-deps"] + list(self.services)
478	        if not exec_command(argv, self.output, cwd=self.project_dir):
479	            raise AppctlError(f"Unable to start the services: {', '.join(self.services)}.")
480	
481	    def _restore_containers(self):
482	        self._restore_files()
483	        self._up()
484	
485	
486	def global_services_dir(environ=None):
487	    environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
488	    return os.path.join(root_dir(environ), GLOBAL_SERVICES_DIR)
489	
490	
491	# -- compose tool ----------------------------------------------------------------------------
492	
493	
494	def compose_version(binary, output=None):
495	    """Installed version of the compose tool ``binary`` (an argv prefix), or ``None``."""
496	    for arguments in (["version", "--short"], ["version"]):
497	        result = run_command(list(binary) + arguments, output)
498	        if result.succeeded and parse_semver(result.stdout):
499	            return _SEMVER_RE.search(result.stdout).group(0).lstrip("v")
500	    return None
501	
502	
503	def compose_download_url(version=COMPOSE_UPGRADE_VERSION, environ=None):
504	    environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
505	    template = environ.get(COMPOSE_URL_ENV) or COMPOSE_URL
506	    machine = platform.machine().lower()
507	    arch = {"amd64": "x86_64", "arm64": "aarch64"}.get(machine, machine)
508	    return template.format(version=version, os=platform.system().lower(), arch=arch)
509	
510	
511	def compose_tool_path(binary, environ=None):
512	    """File to replace: the legacy binary, or the compose CLI plugin."""
513	    environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
514	    if binary[0] == container.LEGACY_COMPOSE_BINARY:
515	        found = shutil.which(container.LEGACY_COMPOSE_BINARY)
516	        return os.path.realpath(found) if found else None
517	    config_dir = environ.get("DOCKER_CONFIG") or os.path.join(os.path.expanduser("~"), ".docker")
518	    user_dir = os.path.join(config_dir, "cli-plugins")
519	    for directory in (user_dir,) + COMPOSE_PLUGIN_DIRS:
520	        candidate = os.path.join(directory, COMPOSE_PLUGIN)
521	        if os.path.isfile(candidate):
522	            return os.path.realpath(candidate)
523	    return os.path.join(user_dir, COMPOSE_PLUGIN)
524	
525	
526	def _remove(path):
527	    if os.path.lexists(path):
528	        os.unlink(path)
529	
530	
531	class ComposeToolUpgrade:
532	    """Replaces a compose tool older than the minimum version, keeping a backup."""
533	
534	    def __init__(self, output=None, environ=None):
535	        self.output = _output(output)
536	        self.environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
537	        self.processor = None
538	        self.path = None
539	        self.existed = False
540	
541	    def run(self):
542	        """Upgrade when needed. Failures restore the old tool and only warn."""
543	        try:
544	            binary = container.compose_binary(self.output)
545	        except AppctlError:
546	            self.output.debug("No compose tool installed, skipping its upgrade.", group="upgrade")
547	            return True
548	        installed = compose_version(binary, self.output)
549	        if installed is None:
550	            self.output.debug("Unable to detect the compose tool version.", group="upgrade")
551	            return True
552	        if compare_semver(installed, MIN_COMPOSE_VERSION) >= 0:
553	            return True
554	        self.path = compose_tool_path(binary, self.environ)
555	        self.existed = bool(self.path) and os.path.exists(self.path)
556	        processor = RevertableStepProcessor(self.output, "compose tool upgrade")
557	        processor.add_step("download compose tool", self._download, self._discard)
558	        processor.add_step("backup compose tool", self._backup, self._restore)
559	        processor.add_step("install compose tool", self._install)
560	        processor.add_step("verify compose tool", self._verify)
561	        ok = processor.execute()
562	        container._compose_binary.clear()
563	        if not ok:
564	            self.output.warning(
565	                f"Unable to upgrade the compose tool from version {installed} to "
566	                f"{COMPOSE_UPGRADE_VERSION}: {processor.error}. Keeping the installed version.")
567	            return True
568	        self.processor = processor
569	        return True
570	
571	    def rollback(self):
572	        if self.processor is not None:
573	            self.processor.rollback()
574	            self.processor = None
575	            container._compose_binary.clear()
576	
577	    def cleanup(self):
578	        if self.processor is not None and self.path:
579	            try:
580	                _remove(self.path + ".backup")
581	            except OSError:
582	                pass
583	
584	    @property
585	    def _new_path(self):
586	        return self.path + ".new"
587	
588	    def _download(self):
589	        if not self.path:
590	            raise AppctlError("Unable to locate the compose tool.")
591	        directory = os.path.dirname(self.path)
592	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
593	        url = compose_download_url(environ=self.environ)
594	        self.output.debug(f"Downloading the compose tool from {url}", group="upgrade")
595	        with urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=120) as response, \
596	                open(self._new_path, "wb") as handle:
597	            shutil.copyfileobj(response, handle)
598	        mode = os.stat(self._new_path).st_mode
599	        os.chmod(self._new_path, mode | stat.S_IXUSR | stat.S_IXGRP | stat.S_IXOTH)
600	        self._check([self._new_path])
601	
602	    def _discard(self):
603	        _remove(self._new_path)
604	
605	    def _backup(self):
606	        if self.existed:
607	            shutil.copy2(self.path, self.path + ".backup")
608	
609	    def _restore(self):
610	        if self.existed:
611	            os.replace(self.path + ".backup", self.path)
612	        else:
613	            _remove(self.path)
614	
615	    def _install(self):
616	        os.replace(self._new_path, self.path)
617	
618	    def _verify(self):
619	        container._compose_binary.clear()
620	        self._check(container.compose_binary(self.output))
621	
622	    def _check(self, binary):
623	        version = compose_version(binary, self.output)
624	        if version is None or compare_semver(version, MIN_COMPOSE_VERSION) < 0:
625	            raise AppctlError(f"The new compose tool reports version {version or 'unknown'}.")
626	
627	
628	# -- pruning ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------
629	
630	
631	def prune_images(targets, output=None):
632	    """Remove old versions of the managed images and dangling appctl images."""
633	    output = _output(output)
634	    ok = True
635	    tags = local_image_tags(output)
636	    for image, target in targets.items():
637	        for tag in sorted(tags.get(image, ())):
638	            if tag != target:
639	                ok = exec_command([container.RUNTIME_BINARY, "rmi", f"{image}:{tag}"],
640	                                  output) and ok
641	    ok = exec_command([container.RUNTIME_BINARY, "image", "prune", "-f", "--filter",
642	                       f"label={container.VENDOR_LABEL}"], output) and ok
643	    if not ok:
644	        output.warning("Unable to prune some old images.")
645	    return ok
646	
647	
648	def prune_networks(output=None):
649	    """Remove unused appctl networks."""
650	    output = _output(output)
651	    ok = exec_command([container.RUNTIME_BINARY, "network", "prune", "-f", "--filter",
652	                       f"label={container.VENDOR_LABEL}"], output)
653	    if not ok:
654	        output.warning("Unable to prune old networks.")
655	    return ok
656	
657	
658	# -- orchestration ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
659	
660	
661	def needs_upgrade(db):
662	    """Whether a recorded appctl version differs from the running one."""
663	    stored = db.get_option(VERSION_OPTION)
664	    return stored is not False and stored != __version__
665	
666	
667	class Upgrade:
668	    def __init__(self, environ=None, output=None, db=None, targets=None):
669	        self.environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
670	        self.output = _output(output)
671	        self.db = db or database.get_db(self.environ)
672	        self.targets = targets
673	        self.changed = {}
674	        self.batches = {}
675	        self.compose_tool = ComposeToolUpgrade(self.output, self.environ)
676	        self.global_upgrade = None
677	        self.project_upgrades = []
678	        self.previous_state = {}
679	
680	    def run(self):
681	        check_disk_space(self.environ, self.output)
682	        if self.targets is None:
683	            self.targets = target_image_versions()
684	        self.targets = dict(sorted(self.targets.items()))
685	        current = current_image_versions(self.db, self.targets, self.output)
686	        self.changed = changed_images(current, self.targets)
687	        processor = RevertableStepProcessor(self.output, "upgrade")
688	        for type in MIGRATION_TYPES:
689	            processor.add_step(f"{type} migrations", self._migrate, self._unmigrate,
690	                               (type,), (type,))
691	        processor.add_step("pull images", pull_images, None, (self.changed, self.output))
692	        processor.add_step("compose tool upgrade", self.compose_tool.run,
693	                           self.compose_tool.rollback)
694	        processor.add_step("global containers", self._upgrade_global, self._revert_global)
695	        processor.add_step("project containers", self._upgrade_projects, self._revert_projects)
696	        processor.add_step("save versions", self._save_state, self._restore_state)
697	        if not processor.execute():
698	            error = processor.error
699	            if not isinstance(error, ReportedError):
700	                reason = error.message if isinstance(error, AppctlError) else str(error)
701	                self.output.error(f"{processor.failed_step.id} failed: {reason or repr(error)}")
702	            raise AppctlError(MIGRATION_ERROR)
703	        self._cleanup()
704	        return True
705	
706	    def _migrate(self, type):
707	        self.batches[type] = MigrationBatch(type, self.db, self.output, self.environ)
708	        self.batches[type].run()
709	
710	    def _unmigrate(self, type):
711	        if type in self.batches:
712	            self.batches.pop(type).rollback()
713	
714	    def _upgrade_global(self):
715	        directory = global_services_dir(self.environ)
716	        if not self.changed or not container.find_base_compose_file(directory):
717	            return
718	        upgrade = ComposeUpgrade("global services", directory, GLOBAL_PROJECT, self.changed,
719	                                 self.output)
720	        if upgrade.needed:
721	            self.global_upgrade = upgrade
722	            upgrade.run()
723	
724	    def _revert_global(self):
725	        if self.global_upgrade is not None:
726	            self.global_upgrade.rollback()
727	            self.global_upgrade = None
728	
729	    def _upgrade_projects(self):
730	        if not self.changed:
731	            return
732	        for project in self.db.get_projects():
733	            path = project["path"]
734	            if not os.path.isdir(path) or not container.find_base_compose_file(path):
735	                self.output.debug(f"Skipping project {project['name']}: no compose file.",
736	                                  group="upgrade")
737	                continue
738	            upgrade = ComposeUpgrade(f"project {project['name']}", path, project["name"],
739	                                     self.changed, self.output)
740	            if not upgrade.needed:
741	                continue
742	            self.project_upgrades.append(upgrade)
743	            upgrade.run()
744	
745	    def _revert_projects(self):
746	        while self.project_upgrades:
747	            self.project_upgrades.pop().rollback()
748	
749	    def _save_state(self):
750	        keys = list(self.targets) + [VERSION_OPTION]
751	        self.previous_state = {key: self.db.get_option(key) for key in keys}
752	        for image, tag in self.targets.items():
753	            self.db.set_option(image, tag)
754	        self.db.set_option(VERSION_OPTION, __version__)
755	
756	    def _restore_state(self):
757	        for key, value in self.previous_state.items():
758	            if value is False:
759	                self.db.delete_option(key)
760	            else:
761	                self.db.set_option(key, value)
762	
763	    def _cleanup(self):
764	        """Cleanup-only work: its failures never fail the upgrade."""
765	        self.compose_tool.cleanup()
766	        if not shutil.which(container.RUNTIME_BINARY):
767	            return
768	        for action, args in ((prune_images, (self.targets, self.output)),
769	                             (prune_networks, (self.output,))):
770	            try:
771	                action(*args)
772	            except Exception as exc:  # pruning is best effort
773	                self.output.warning(f"Unable to prune: {exc}")
774	
775	
776	def run_upgrade(environ=None, output=None):
777	    return Upgrade(environ, output).run()

"""Extraction of ``.zip`` and ``.tar.gz`` archives into a directory."""

import os
import shutil
import stat
import tarfile
import tempfile

from .errors import AppctlError
from .process import run_command

try:
    import zipfile
except ImportError:  # pragma: no cover - depends on the Python build
    zipfile = None

UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE = "Extraction only supported for '.zip' and '.tar.gz' file types."


def archive_type(path):
    """``"zip"``, ``"tar.gz"`` or ``None`` for an unsupported extension."""
    name = str(path).lower()
    if name.endswith(".zip"):
        return "zip"
    if name.endswith(".tar.gz"):
        return "tar.gz"
    return None


def validate_archive(path):
    """Raise unless ``path`` names an existing archive of a supported type."""
    if path is None or path is True or path is False or str(path) == "":
        raise AppctlError("Please provide the archive to extract with --archive=<archive-path>.")
    kind = archive_type(path)
    if kind is None:
        raise AppctlError(UNSUPPORTED_MESSAGE)
    if not os.path.exists(path):
        raise AppctlError(f"Archive '{path}' does not exist.")
    if not os.path.isfile(path):
        raise AppctlError(f"Archive '{path}' is not a file.")
    if not os.access(path, os.R_OK):
        raise AppctlError(f"Archive '{path}' is not readable.")
    return kind


def _extract_zip(archive, target):
    if zipfile is None:
        raise AppctlError("Extracting a zip file requires the 'zipfile' module to be available.")
    try:
        with zipfile.ZipFile(archive) as bundle:
            bundle.extractall(target)
    except (zipfile.BadZipFile, zipfile.LargeZipFile, OSError, ValueError, RuntimeError) as exc:
        raise AppctlError(f"Unable to extract '{archive}': {exc}") from exc


def _extract_tarball(archive, target, output):
    try:
        with tarfile.open(archive, "r:gz") as bundle:
            bundle.extractall(target, filter="data")
        return

from .process import warn_signal_exit

SSH_BINARY_ENV = "APPCTL_SSH_BINARY"

SSH_URL_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(?:(?P<scheme>docker|docker-compose|docker-compose-run|ssh|vagrant):(?://)?)?"

    r"(?P<host>[^:/~]+)"

    r"(?P<path>[/~].*)?$"
)

    """Split ``[scheme:][user@]host[:port][path]`` into its components."""
    match = SSH_URL_RE.match(str(url).strip())
    if not match:
        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid SSH connection string '{url}'.")
    return {k: v for k, v in match.groupdict().items() if v}

    stripped = []
    end_of_options = False
    for token in argv:
        if token == END_OF_OPTIONS:
            end_of_options = True
        elif not end_of_options and is_assoc_token(token) and parse_assoc_token(token)[0] == "ssh":
            continue
        stripped.append(token)
    return stripped


def build_remote_command(argv, environ, alias=None, alias_params=None, path=None):
    """The shell command run on the remote side."""
    binary = environ.get(SSH_BINARY_ENV) or PROGRAM_NAME
    prefix = ""
    pre_cmd = (environ.get(SSH_PRE_CMD_ENV) or "").strip().rstrip(";").strip()
    if pre_cmd:
        prefix = pre_cmd + "; "
    words = []
    if alias:
        forwarded = {k: v for k, v in (alias_params or {}).items() if k != "ssh"}
        if forwarded:
            encoded = json.dumps({alias: forwarded}, separators=(",", ":"))
            prefix += f"APPCTL_RUNTIME_ALIAS={shlex.quote(encoded)} "
            words.append(alias)
    words.extend(_strip_ssh_flags(argv))
    if path:
        words.append(f"--path={path}")
    return prefix + " ".join([binary] + [shlex.quote(w) for w in words])


def build_transport(bits, remote_command, tty=False, proxyjump=None, key=None):
    """argv of the local process that carries ``remote_command``."""
    scheme = bits.get("scheme", "ssh")
    host = bits["host"]
    user = bits.get("user")
    if scheme == "docker":
        argv = ["docker", "exec"]
        if user:
            argv += ["--user", user]
        argv += ["-it" if tty else "-i", host, "sh", "-c", remote_command]
        return argv
    if scheme in ("docker-compose", "docker-compose-run"):
        argv = ["docker-compose", "exec" if scheme == "docker-compose" else "run"]
        if user:

            argv.append("-T")
        if scheme == "docker-compose-run":
            argv.append("--rm")

    return stream is None or stream is default


def run_remote(ssh, argv, environ, output, alias=None, alias_params=None, skip_tty=False):

    bits = parse_ssh_url(ssh)
    alias_params = alias_params or {}
    remote_command = build_remote_command(argv, environ, alias, alias_params, bits.get("path"))
    passthrough = _real_stream(output.stdout, sys.stdout) and _real_stream(output.stderr, sys.stderr)
    tty = bool(passthrough and not skip_tty and sys.stdout.isatty() and sys.stdin.isatty())
    transport = build_transport(bits, remote_command, tty=tty,
                                proxyjump=alias_params.get("proxyjump"),
                                key=alias_params.get("key"))

            output.stderr.write(result.stderr)
            code = result.returncode
    except OSError:
        code = CONNECTION_FAILED
    warn_signal_exit(code, output)
    if code == CONNECTION_FAILED:
        raise AppctlError("Cannot connect over SSH using provided configuration.", CONNECTION_FAILED)
    return code

class RevertableTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_rollback_reverse_and_continue(self):
        events = []
        stderr = io.StringIO()
        processor = RevertableStepProcessor(Output(stderr=stderr, stdout=io.StringIO()))

        def fail():
            raise RuntimeError("nope")

        def bad_undo():
            events.append("undo b")
            raise RuntimeError("undo failed")

        processor.add_step("a", lambda: events.append("a"), lambda: events.append("undo a"))
        processor.add_step("b", lambda: events.append("b"), bad_undo)
        processor.add_step("c", lambda: events.append("c"))
        processor.add_step("d", fail, lambda: events.append("undo d"))
        processor.add_step("e", lambda: events.append("e"), lambda: events.append("undo e"))
        self.assertFalse(processor.execute())
        self.assertEqual(events, ["a", "b", "c", "undo d", "undo b", "undo a"])
        self.assertIn("Unable to roll back step 'b': undo failed", stderr.getvalue())
        self.assertEqual(str(processor.error), "nope")

    def test_false_return_fails(self):
        processor = RevertableStepProcessor()
        processor.add_step("x", lambda: False)
        self.assertFalse(processor.execute())

import hashlib
import os
import re
import shutil
import sys
import tempfile

from .config_loader import ROOT_DIR_ENV, root_dir

CACHE_DIR_ENV = "APPCTL_CACHE_DIR"
CACHE_TTL_ENV = "APPCTL_CACHE_TTL"
CACHE_MAX_SIZE_ENV = "APPCTL_CACHE_MAX_SIZE"

DEFAULT_TTL = 180 * 86400               # 180 days, in seconds
DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE = 300 * 1024 * 1024    # 300 MiB, in bytes
MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH = 120
HASH_LENGTH = 12

_UNSAFE_RE = re.compile(r"[^A-Za-z0-9._-]")
_URL_SCHEME_RE = re.compile(r"^[A-Za-z][A-Za-z0-9+.-]*://")


def cache_dir(environ=None):
    """``APPCTL_CACHE_DIR``, otherwise ``<APPCTL_ROOT_DIR>/.cache/``."""
    environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
    value = environ.get(CACHE_DIR_ENV)
    if value:
        return value
    return os.path.join(root_dir(environ), ".cache") + os.sep


def _int_setting(environ, name, default):
    try:
        value = int(str(environ.get(name, "")).strip())
    except ValueError:
        return default
    return value if value >= 0 else default


def _digest(text):
    return hashlib.sha256(text.encode("utf-8", "surrogatepass")).hexdigest()[:HASH_LENGTH]


def _sanitize_segment(segment):
    """Make one path segment filesystem-safe; altered segments get a hash suffix."""
    safe = _UNSAFE_RE.sub("-", segment)
    if safe in ("", ".", ".."):
        safe = safe.replace(".", "-") or "-"
    if safe != segment or len(safe) > MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH:
        safe = f"{safe[:MAX_SEGMENT_LENGTH]}-{_digest(segment)}"
    return safe


def sanitize_key(key):
    """Map a cache key to a deterministic, filesystem-safe relative path.

    URL keys are stored under ``misc/<scheme>-<host>[-<port>]/<path>[-<query>]``;
    other keys keep their ``/``-separated structure. Any segment that has to be
    altered gets a hash of its original value appended, so distinct keys do not
    collide.
    """
    key = str(key).strip()
    if _URL_SCHEME_RE.match(key):
        url = urlsplit(key)
        host = url.hostname or ""
        try:
            port = url.port
        except ValueError:
            port = None
        location = f"{url.scheme}-{host}" + (f"-{port}" if port else "")
        resource = url.path.lstrip("/") + (f"-{url.query}" if url.query else "")
        parts = ["misc", location] + [p for p in resource.split("/") if p]
        if len(parts) == 2:
            parts.append("-")
    else:
        parts = [p for p in key.replace("\\", "/").split("/") if p]
    if not parts:
        return _sanitize_segment("")
    return "/".join(_sanitize_segment(part) for part in parts)


def _warn(output, text):
    if output is not None:
        output.warning(text)
    else:
        print(f"Warning: {text}", file=sys.stderr)


class FileCache:
    """Key/value file store with a TTL and a maximum total size."""

    def __init__(self, root, ttl=DEFAULT_TTL, max_size=DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE, output=None):
        self.configured_root = str(root)
        self.root = os.path.join(self.configured_root, "")
        self.ttl = int(ttl)
        self.max_size = int(max_size)
        self.output = output
        self.enabled = self._ensure_dir_exists(self.root, self.configured_root)

    def _ensure_dir_exists(self, directory, label=None):
        if os.path.isdir(directory):
            return True
        try:
            os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            reason = exc.strerror or exc
            _warn(self.output, f"Failed to create directory '{label or directory}': {reason}.")
            return False
        return True

    def is_enabled(self):
        return self.enabled

    def get_root(self):
        return self.root

    else:

    if not parts:
        return _sanitize_segment("")
    return "/".join(_sanitize_segment(part) for part in parts)


def _warn(output, text):
    if output is not None:
        output.warning(text)
    else:
        print(f"Warning: {text}", file=sys.stderr)


class FileCache:
    """Key/value file store with a TTL and a maximum total size."""

    def __init__(self, root, ttl=DEFAULT_TTL, max_size=DEFAULT_MAX_SIZE, output=None):
        self.configured_root = str(root)
        self.root = os.path.join(self.configured_root, "")
        self.ttl = int(ttl)
        self.max_size = int(max_size)
        self.output = output
        self.enabled = self._ensure_dir_exists(self.root, self.configured_root)

    def _ensure_dir_exists(self, directory, label=None):
        if os.path.isdir(directory):
            return True
        try:
            os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
        except OSError as exc:
            reason = exc.strerror or exc
            _warn(self.output, f"Failed to create directory '{label or directory}': {reason}.")
            return False
        return True

    def is_enabled(self):
        return self.enabled

    def get_root(self):
        return self.root

        comparison = 0 if str(stored) == str(current) else 1
    if comparison > 0:
        return VERSION_NEWER
    if comparison < 0:
        return VERSION_OLDER
    return VERSION_CURRENT


def stored_version(db):
    """The persisted appctl version, or ``None`` before the first run."""
    stored = db.get_option(VERSION_OPTION)
    return None if stored is False else stored


def needs_upgrade(db):
    """Whether the stored version calls for a migration of the running binary."""
    stored = stored_version(db)
    return stored is not None and version_status(stored) == VERSION_NEWER

class Setup:
    """First-run setup: run every pending migration, then record the version."""

    def __init__(self, environ=None, output=None, db=None):
        self.environ = os.environ if environ is None else environ
        self.output = _output(output)
        self.db = db or database.get_db(self.environ)
        self.batches = {}

    def run(self):
        processor = RevertableStepProcessor(self.output, "setup")
        for type in MIGRATION_TYPES:
            processor.add_step(f"{type} migrations", self._migrate, self._unmigrate,
                               (type,), (type,))
        processor.add_step("save version", self.db.set_option, self.db.delete_option,
                           (VERSION_OPTION, __version__), (VERSION_OPTION,))
        if not processor.execute():
            error = processor.error
            if not isinstance(error, ReportedError):
                reason = error.message if isinstance(error, AppctlError) else str(error)
                self.output.error(f"{processor.failed_step.id} failed: {reason or repr(error)}")
            raise AppctlError(MIGRATION_ERROR)
        return True

    def _migrate(self, type):
        self.batches[type] = MigrationBatch(type, self.db, self.output, self.environ)
        self.batches[type].run()

    def _unmigrate(self, type):
        if type in self.batches:
            self.batches.pop(type).rollback()


def run_setup(environ=None, output=None, db=None):

"""Multi-step operations that undo their completed steps when one step fails."""

from dataclasses import dataclass, field


@dataclass
class Step:
    id: str
    up: object
    down: object = None
    up_args: tuple = field(default_factory=tuple)
    down_args: tuple = field(default_factory=tuple)


class StepFailed(Exception):
    """A step returned ``False``."""


class RevertableStepProcessor:
    """Runs steps in order; on failure, undoes them in reverse order.

    A step fails when ``up`` raises or returns ``False``. The undo of the
    failed step runs too, so a step can clean up its own partial work.
    Undo failures are logged and the rollback continues; steps without an
    undo action are skipped silently. A processor that succeeded can still
    be rolled back later with :meth:`rollback`.
    """

    def __init__(self, output=None, name=None):
        self.output = output
        self.name = name
        self.steps = []
        self.executed = []
        self.error = None
        self.failed_step = None

    def add_step(self, step_id, up, down=None, up_args=(), down_args=()):
        self.steps.append(Step(str(step_id), up, down, tuple(up_args), tuple(down_args)))
        return self

    def _log(self, text):
        if self.output is not None:
            self.output.debug(text, group="upgrade")
            if self.output.logger is not None:
                self.output.logger.write(text)

    def _warn(self, text):
        if self.output is not None:
            self.output.warning(text)

"""``appctl cli``: information about appctl itself and its self-management."""

import json
import os
import platform
import pprint
import shutil

from .. import PROGRAM_NAME, __version__, container, database, upgrade
from ..arguments import is_assoc_token, parse_assoc_token
from ..config_loader import ALL_ALIAS, alias_sort_key, is_alias, packages_dir, root_dir
from ..errors import AppctlError
from ..extract import extract_archive, validate_archive
from ..file_cache import cache_dir
from ..formatter import format_value, to_json, to_yaml
from ..process import exec_command, run_command
from ..resolver import try_resolve
from ..runtime_config import GLOBAL_PARAMETERS, visible_parameters
from ..self_update import (UPDATE_ALL_FIELDS, UPDATE_FIELDS, available_updates,
                           selected_update_type, self_update, up_to_date_message)
from ..synopsis import ASSOC, FLAG, POSITIONAL
from ..system import (INSTALL_DIR, PRODUCT_NAME, archive_path, binary_path, ensure_requirements,
                      runtime_binary, runtime_binary_path, runtime_version)
from ._listing import LIST_OPTIONS, render_list

INFO_FORMATS = ("list", "json")
CHECK_UPDATE_FORMATS = ("table", "csv", "json", "count", "yaml")
PARAM_DUMP_FORMATS = ("json", "var_export")
ALIAS_FORMATS = ("yaml", "json")
SHELLS = ("bash", "zsh")

ALL_ALIAS_DESCRIPTION = "Run command against every registered alias."
FILE_MARKER = "<file> "
FILE_DESCRIPTION = "Path to a file."
UNINSTALL_QUESTION = (f"Are you sure you want to remove {PRODUCT_NAME} and all its projects "
                      "(along with their data)? This is an irreversible action. "
                      "No backup will be kept.")


def _environ(ctx):
    return ctx.environ if ctx.environ is not None else os.environ


def _check_format(fmt, allowed):
    if fmt not in allowed:
        raise AppctlError(f"Invalid format: {fmt}. Supported formats: {', '.join(allowed)}.")


# -- version / info ----------------------------------------------------------------


def version(ctx, args, assoc):
    ctx.output.line(__version__)


def _os_description():
    parts = (platform.system(), platform.release(), platform.version(), platform.machine())
    return " ".join(part for part in parts if part)


def info_data(ctx):
    environ = _environ(ctx)
    packages = packages_dir(environ)
    packages = packages if os.path.isdir(packages) else None
    config = ctx.config
    try:
        stored = upgrade.stored_version(database.get_db(environ))
    except AppctlError:
        stored = None
    return {
        "os": _os_description(),
        "shell": environ.get("SHELL") or environ.get("COMSPEC"),
        "runtime_binary": runtime_binary(environ),
        "runtime_binary_path": runtime_binary_path(environ),
        "runtime_version": runtime_version(environ),
        "python_version": platform.python_version(),
        "appctl_dir_path": INSTALL_DIR,
        "appctl_binary_path": binary_path(),
        "appctl_archive_path": archive_path(),
        "appctl_root_dir": root_dir(environ),
        "appctl_packages_dir_path": packages,
        "packages_dir": packages,
        "appctl_cache_dir": cache_dir(environ),
        "global_config_path": config.global_path if config else None,
        "project_config_path": config.project_path if config else None,
        "appctl_version": __version__,
        "appctl_stored_version": stored,
        "appctl_nightly": upgrade.is_nightly(),
        "release_channel": ctx.runtime.get("installer_version"),
        "strict_args_mode": ctx.strict,
        "runtime_config": {k: v for k, v in ctx.runtime.items()
                           if k in GLOBAL_PARAMETERS and v != GLOBAL_PARAMETERS[k].default},
    }


INFO_LABELS = (
    ("os", "OS"),
    ("shell", "Shell"),
    ("runtime_binary", "Runtime binary"),
    ("runtime_binary_path", "Runtime binary path"),
    ("runtime_version", "Runtime version"),
    ("appctl_dir_path", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} dir path"),
    ("appctl_binary_path", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} binary path"),
    ("appctl_archive_path", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} archive path"),
    ("appctl_root_dir", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} root dir"),
    ("appctl_packages_dir_path", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} packages dir"),
    ("appctl_cache_dir", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} cache dir"),
    ("global_config_path", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} global config"),
    ("project_config_path", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} project config"),
    ("appctl_version", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} version"),
    ("appctl_stored_version", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} stored version"),
    ("appctl_nightly", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} nightly build"),
    ("release_channel", f"{PRODUCT_NAME} release channel"),
    ("strict_args_mode", "Strict args mode"),
)


def _info_text(value):
    if value is None:
        return ""
    if isinstance(value, bool):
        return "yes" if value else "no"
    return format_value(value)


def info(ctx, args, assoc):
    fmt = assoc.get("format", "list")
    _check_format(fmt, INFO_FORMATS)
    data = info_data(ctx)
    if fmt == "json":
        ctx.output.line(json.dumps(data, indent=4, default=str))
        return
    for key, label in INFO_LABELS:
        ctx.output.line(f"{label}:\t{_info_text(data[key])}")
    for key, value in data["runtime_config"].items():
        ctx.output.line(f"--{key}:\t{format_value(value)}")


# -- updates ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def extract(ctx, assoc):
    """``cli update --archive``: extract a local ``.zip``/``.tar.gz`` into a directory."""
    archive = assoc.get("archive")
    validate_archive(archive)
    dest = assoc.get("path") or ctx.runtime.get("path") or os.getcwd()
    if dest is True:
        raise AppctlError("--path parameter needs a value.")
    dest = extract_archive(archive, str(dest), ctx.output)
    ctx.output.success(f"Extracted '{archive}' to '{dest}'.")


def update(ctx, args, assoc):
    if "archive" in assoc:
        return extract(ctx, assoc)
    return self_update(_environ(ctx), ctx.output, assoc, ctx.argv)


def check_update(ctx, args, assoc):
    fmt = assoc.get("format") or "table"
    _check_format(fmt, CHECK_UPDATE_FORMATS)
    only = selected_update_type(ctx.argv, assoc)
    updates = available_updates(_environ(ctx), __version__, only)
    if not updates and fmt == "table":
        ctx.output.success(up_to_date_message(only))
        return
    render_list(ctx, updates, dict(assoc, format=fmt), UPDATE_FIELDS, UPDATE_ALL_FIELDS,
                id_field="version", single_as_item=False)


def migrate(ctx, args, assoc):
    upgrade.run_upgrade(ctx.environ, ctx.output)
    ctx.output.success(f"Upgraded to {PROGRAM_NAME} {__version__}.")


# -- dumps ------------------------------------------------------------------------------


def param_dump(ctx, args, assoc):
    fmt = assoc.get("format", "json")
    _check_format(fmt, PARAM_DUMP_FORMATS)
    parameters = visible_parameters()
    dump = {}
    for name in sorted(parameters):
        param = parameters[name]
        entry = {
            "runtime": param.runtime,
            "file": param.file,
            "synopsis": param.synopsis,
            "default": param.default,
            "multiple": param.multiple,
            "description": param.description,
            "deprecated": param.deprecated,
        }
        if assoc.get("with-values"):
            entry["current"] = ctx.runtime.get(name)
        dump[name] = entry
    if fmt == "var_export":
        ctx.output.line(pprint.pformat(dump, sort_dicts=False))
    else:
        ctx.output.line(json.dumps(dump, indent=4, default=str))


def command_to_dict(command):
    entry = {
        "name": command.name,
        "description": command.description,
        "longdesc": command.longdesc or "",
        "subcommands": [command_to_dict(sub) for sub in command.sorted_subcommands()],
    }
    if not entry["subcommands"]:
        entry["synopsis"] = command.synopsis
    return entry


def cmd_dump(ctx, args, assoc):
    ctx.output.line(to_json(command_to_dict(ctx.root)))


def has_command(ctx, args, assoc):
    tokens = " ".join(str(arg) for arg in args).split()
    if not tokens:
        return 1
    resolved = try_resolve(ctx.root, tokens)
    if resolved is None or resolved[1]:
        return 1
    disabled = {" ".join(str(entry).split()) for entry in ctx.runtime.get("disabled_commands", ())}
    path = resolved[0].path
    if any(" ".join(path[:depth]) in disabled for depth in range(1, len(path) + 1)):
        return 1
    return 0


# -- aliases ----------------------------------------------------------------------------


def alias_listing(aliases):
    """Registered aliases by name; ``@all`` first when registered."""
    listing = {}
    if ALL_ALIAS in aliases:
        definition = aliases[ALL_ALIAS]
        listing[ALL_ALIAS] = ALL_ALIAS_DESCRIPTION if definition is None else definition
    for name in sorted((n for n in aliases if n != ALL_ALIAS), key=alias_sort_key):
        listing[name] = aliases[name]
    return listing


def alias(ctx, args, assoc):
    fmt = assoc.get("format", "yaml")
    _check_format(fmt, ALIAS_FORMATS)
    listing = alias_listing(ctx.config.aliases if ctx.config else {})
    ctx.output.line(to_json(listing) if fmt == "json" else to_yaml(listing))


# -- self-uninstall ----------------------------------------------------------------------

RESOURCES = (
    ("containers", ["ps", "-aq"], ["rm", "-f"]),
    ("networks", ["network", "ls", "-q"], ["network", "rm"]),
    ("volumes", ["volume", "ls", "-q"], ["volume", "rm", "-f"]),
    ("images", ["images", "-q"], ["rmi", "-f"]),
)


def _labeled_ids(list_command, output):
    argv = [container.RUNTIME_BINARY] + list_command + ["--filter",
                                                        f"label={container.VENDOR_LABEL}"]
    result = run_command(argv, output)
    if not result.succeeded:
        return None
    ids = []
    for item in result.stdout.split():
        if item not in ids:
            ids.append(item)
    return ids


def remove_runtime_resources(output):
    """Remove every appctl-labeled container, network, volume and image."""
    for kind, list_command, remove_command in RESOURCES:
        ids = _labeled_ids(list_command, output)
        if ids is None:
            output.warning(f"Unable to list the {PRODUCT_NAME} {kind}.")
            continue
        if ids and not exec_command([container.RUNTIME_BINARY] + remove_command + ids, output):
            output.warning(f"Unable to remove some {PRODUCT_NAME} {kind}.")


def _is_protected(path):
    path = os.path.realpath(path)
    protected = {os.path.realpath(os.sep), os.path.realpath(os.path.expanduser("~"))}
    return path in protected


def _remove_tree(path, output):
    if not path or not os.path.lexists(path):
        return
    if _is_protected(path):
        output.warning(f"Refusing to remove '{path}'.")
        return
    try:
        if os.path.isdir(path) and not os.path.islink(path):
            shutil.rmtree(path)
        else:
            os.unlink(path)
    except OSError as exc:
        output.warning(f"Unable to remove '{path}': {exc.strerror or exc}.")


def self_uninstall(ctx, args, assoc):
    environ = _environ(ctx)
    output = ctx.output
    ensure_requirements(environ, output)
    if not output.confirm(UNINSTALL_QUESTION, assoc):
        return 0
    remove_runtime_resources(output)
    try:
        projects = database.get_db(environ).get_projects()
    except AppctlError as exc:
        output.warning(f"Unable to read the projects: {exc.message}")
        projects = []
    database.close_all()
    for project in projects:
        _remove_tree(project["path"], output)
    if output.logger is not None:
        output.logger.enabled = False
    _remove_tree(root_dir(environ), output)
    archive = archive_path()
    if archive:
        _remove_tree(archive, output)
    output.success(f"{PRODUCT_NAME} has been removed successfully.")
    return 0


# -- tab completion -------------------------------------------------------------------------


def _completion_words(line):
    """Split the line into completed words and the word being typed."""
    words = line.split()
    current = words.pop() if words and not line[-1].isspace() else ""
    if words and os.path.basename(words[0]) in (PROGRAM_NAME, f"{PROGRAM_NAME}.py"):
        words = words[1:]
    elif not words and os.path.basename(current) in (PROGRAM_NAME, f"{PROGRAM_NAME}.py"):
        current = ""
    return words, current


def _alias_description(definition):
    if definition is None:
        return ALL_ALIAS_DESCRIPTION
    if isinstance(definition, list):
        return "Group of aliases: " + ", ".join(definition)
    if isinstance(definition, dict):
        target = definition.get("ssh") or definition.get("path") or definition.get("url")
        if target:
            return f"Alias for {target}."
    return "Alias."


def _is_file_positional(token):
    name = (token.name or "").lower()
    return name == "file" or name.endswith(("-file", "_file"))


def completion_suggestions(root, line, aliases=None):
    """``[(suggestion, description)]`` for the word at the end of ``line``, sorted."""
    words, current = _completion_words(line)
    alias_given = bool(words) and is_alias(words[0])
    if alias_given:
        words = words[1:]
    used = {parse_assoc_token(w)[0] for w in words if is_assoc_token(w)}
    command = root
    consumed = True
    positional_count = 0
    for word in (w for w in words if not is_assoc_token(w)):
        child = command.find_subcommand(word) if consumed else None
        if child is None:
            if not command.is_runnable or command.is_root:
                return []
            consumed = False
            positional_count += 1
            continue
        command = child

    found = {}

    def add(text, description=""):
        if text.startswith(current):
            found.setdefault(text, description or "")

    if consumed and command.is_root and not alias_given:
        for name, definition in (aliases or {}).items():
            add(f"{name} ", _alias_description(definition))
    if consumed:
        for sub in command.sorted_subcommands():
            add(f"{sub.name} ", sub.description)
    if command.is_runnable and not command.is_root:
        positionals = command.tokens_of_type(POSITIONAL)
        upcoming = None
        if positional_count < len(positionals):
            upcoming = positionals[positional_count]
        elif positionals and positionals[-1].repeating:
            upcoming = positionals[-1]
        if upcoming is not None and _is_file_positional(upcoming) and not current.startswith("-"):
            return [(FILE_MARKER, FILE_DESCRIPTION)]
        for token in command.tokens_of_type(ASSOC, FLAG):
            if token.name not in used:
                text = f"--{token.name}=" if token.type == ASSOC else f"--{token.name} "
                add(text, command.options.get(token.name, ""))
        for name, param in visible_parameters().items():
            if param.runtime and name not in used:
                add(f"--{name}=" if "=" in param.synopsis else f"--{name} ", param.description)
    return sorted(found.items(), key=lambda item: (item[0].lower(), item[0]))


def render_completion(suggestion, description, shell="bash"):
    if shell != "zsh":
        return suggestion
    name = suggestion.rstrip().replace("\\", "\\\\").replace(":", "\\:")
    summary = " ".join(str(description or "").split())
